history.summary: The Twin Ganesha temple of Barsur houses two remarkable monolithic sandstone idols of Lord Ganesha, one about 7.5 feet tall (locally claimed to be the third-largest Ganesha statue in the world — claim unverified) and the other about 5.5 feet. The original temple structure has been lost to time; the surviving idols now stand under a newly constructed mandapam fortified with grills on all sides, with remnants of pillars, stones and damaged sculptures scattered nearby. Local legend says Banasura built the twin temple at the wish of his daughter and her friend, as an act of devotion. Barsur itself was the 11th-century capital of the Nagavanshi rulers. ASI-protected site. (CSV town 'Jagdalpur' is wrong — the temple is at Barsur in Dantewada district, ~75 km SW of Jagdalpur. Coordinates are approximate — temple-specific coordinates are not published by reliable sources.)

name: Ganesha Temple
town_description: Barsur is an ancient town in Dantewada district on the banks of the Indravati river, about 75-80 km southwest of Jagdalpur. It was the 11th-century capital of the Nagavanshi (Chindaka Naga) kings, and local tradition credits it with 147 temples and 147 tanks at its zenith. Today it is a quiet rural town whose scattered ASI-protected ruins — the Battisa, Mama-Bhanja and twin-Ganesha temples — make it the richest archaeological zone of Bastar.
